hook: The first full-length structure of human hephaestin shows a membrane-anchored homodimer at 2.3 angstroms.
summary: Hephaestin helps move iron out of gut cells. The authors purified the full-length human protein and solved its cryo-EM structure, a stable homodimer with a negatively charged funnel leading to the substrate site that may capture Fe2+. The membrane helices are less well resolved, and how it works with ferroportin was not tested.
title: Structure of human hephaestin reveals a homodimer anchored to the cell membrane
